note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The differences from A. aneristus are given under that species: the alate has a smaller fontanelle, smaller ocelli farther from the compound eyes and a more inflated postclypeus, and the worker has a short midgut–hindgut junction situated to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot and a ventrally placed, distinctly trilobed enteric valve seat. In A. hilarus the alate fontanelle is larger, the postclypeus shorter and the mandibular apical tooth longer, the worker apical tooth is also long, and the midgut–hindgut overlap is longer. A. mansuetus has a large, circular, flat fontanelle and slightly different alate mandibular proportions; its worker has a longer apical tooth, and the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible only just clears the molar prominence. In A. pacatus the alate compound eyes and ocelli are large, and the worker has a slender fore tibia, a bilobed enteric valve seat and different mandibular proportions. A. prosenus is larger, with longer apical teeth in both castes, a shallow fontanelle and even pilosity in the alate, and a slender fore tibia in the worker.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity rather dense, quite short, yellow. Postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.24, Pcl/Ri 1.73. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.58, Ra/Ri 0.75; a broad, deep notch, in surface view, separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence, L4/L1·Lm 9.10; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Rj·Rm 11.91. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 4.54; third apical spur about half the length of the other two but pale and inconspicuous. The midgut–hindgut overlap is oblique or slightly flat and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is ventral, distinctly trilobed, the third inner lobe somewhat smaller, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a distinct neck; no discernible minute spines were observed on the valve membrane outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark chestnut brown, jet black above the ocelli; fontanelle less than half the ocellus, slightly irregularly elliptical, slightly concave or with a median ridge, dark chestnut brown; central spot as large as the fontanelle, slightly raised or nearly flat, short-elliptical, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus dark brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal groove distinct, slightly concave, semicircular, dark chestnut brown; antennae brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum chestnut brown, the dark transverse sutures distinct; femora dark brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles dark brown, ventral spiracles and lateral parts of the sternites brown, the median part of the sternites paler; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli rather small, their distance from the compound eye about equal to their minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.27–0.28, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture very distinct. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.49–0.66, Ra/Rj 0.69–0.70; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is remote from the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 5.63–6.06; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal in length. Meso- and metanotum moderately broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30–0.31. Cephalic pilosity brown, uneven, without a hair layer.
